decisions.statement: Every address handed in is restated over one reading of the bodies.
The module restating addresses is called rather than reached through a rung.
That restating comes before any page is renamed.
Each page's own rename is left to the change renaming one page.
That change is told the addresses are restated already.
A page handed in under the slug that page carries has no address restated.
A page's slug and page type are read from that page's body rather than its name.
A body that cannot be read refuses the whole answer.
A call handing in no page is refused.
The first refusal answers for the whole call.

definition: many pages renamed over one reading of the bodies naming them
